function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—rather it emerged from the work of many thinkers and experimenters over several centuries:

| Era | Key Contributors | What They Did |
|-----|------------------|---------------|
| **Ancient & Renaissance** | *Thales of Miletus* (~600 BCE), *William Gilbert* (late‑1500s) | First noted static attraction (“Greek fire”) and coined the word *electrum*. Gilbert’s book _De Magnete_ laid groundwork for electrical science. |
| **18th Century – Early Experiments** | *Charles François de Cisternay du Fay*, *Benjamin Franklin*, *Alessandro Volta* | Du Fay showed positive/negative charges; Franklin conducted kite experiments and proposed charge polarity; Volta invented the voltaic pile—the first battery. |
| **19th Century – Systematic Study** | *Hans Christian Ørsted*, *Michael Faraday*, *James Clerk Maxwell* | Ørsted linked magnetism and electricity; Faraday formulated electromagnetic induction; Maxwell unified electromagnetism into equations predicting light waves. |

So while no single discoverer exists, figures such as William Gilbert, Benjamin Franklin, Alessandro Volta, Hans Christian Ørsted, Michael Faraday, and James Clerk Maxwell were pivotal in turning observations of static sparks into the modern understanding of electricity.
